name: contoso-oil-rag-ladder
description: Corpus-grounded evaluation of the RAG ladder over the 25-document Contoso Oil corpus: plain RAG, a fixed contract-filtered RAG, an unfiltered smart-index control, a classifier-routed type filter and an oracle type filter. Queries are stratified into contract questions with competing wrong-type documents (contract_distractor), contract questions without meaningful competition (contract_clean), questions whose authoritative answer lives in another document type (other_type) and questions the corpus cannot answer or that carry a false premise (unanswerable). Each query lists verbatim evidence, required facts with paraphrase alternatives and, where relevant, distractor documents and facts that a correct answer never needs to state. References, target types and labels are evaluation-only and are never agent, router or index input. The dev split may be inspected while iterating; the test split is the headline result. v2.1 (2026-11-18, before any test-split answers were generated): required/distractor facts reduced to necessary, short canonical cores after a dev-split pipeline check showed paraphrase misses.
hypotheses: H1: On contract_distractor, the contract-filtered and routed variants cite fewer wrong-type documents, mention fewer distractor facts and recover at least as many required facts as plain RAG.
H2: On other_type, the fixed contract filter loses required facts relative to plain RAG, while the routed variant does not.
H3: The unfiltered smart-index control matches plain RAG on every stratum; re-indexing alone yields no gain.
H4: The oracle type filter bounds the routed variant from above; the gap between them measures router error.

strata.contract_distractor: Authoritative answer is in one or more signed contracts, and at least one non-contract document (policy, training or planning deck, invoice, letter, email, memo, draft heads of terms or a document with embedded instructions) contains similar wording with different values or non-binding statements.
strata.contract_clean: Authoritative answer is in a contract and no other document type offers meaningfully competing text; metadata filtering should neither help nor hurt.
strata.other_type: Authoritative answer is in an invoice, policy, technical report, correspondence or presentation; contracts or other types may be lexically similar distractors. A fixed contract filter removes the answer.
strata.unanswerable: The corpus does not contain the requested value or the question carries a false premise. A good answer checks the listed documents, says what is absent or corrects the premise, and does not import values from neighbouring documents.

queries.query: What payment terms apply under our supplier contracts?

evidence.doc-001: within forty-five (45) days of receipt of invoice
evidence.doc-004: payment is due thirty (30) days after the end of the month
evidence.doc-021: within thirty (30) days of the invoice date

required_facts: 60 days from the end of the month
60 days after the end of the month
queries.ground_truth: Northwind vessel charter: 45 days from receipt. Fabrikam rig maintenance: 30 days after the end of the month a valid invoice is received. Litware drilling consumables: 60 days end of month. Proseware pipeline inspection: 30 days from receipt of undisputed milestone invoices. Fourth Coffee catering: 30 days from receipt of a valid monthly invoice. Tailspin helicopter: 30 days from invoice date. These differ from training aspirations or procurement defaults.
queries.expected_behavior: Search and cite the supplier agreements. Distinguish each supplier's payment trigger. Do not present net 15 or net 90 from a training presentation, or the policy default, as signed terms.
